oauth.notes: HubSpot's current developer platform builds apps as 'projects' with the HubSpot CLI.

verdict.summary: No approval is needed to start, but the app is built with a command-line tool rather than a web form, and installers see an 'unverified app' checkbox until you are listed in HubSpot's Marketplace.

whoYouNeed.why: Apps are created and uploaded from a developer account using the HubSpot CLI.

whoYouNeed.role: A Super Admin in each customer's HubSpot account
whoYouNeed.why: HubSpot only lets Super Admins install apps.

steps.title: Sign in to HubSpot's developer account and the CLI
steps.plain: Log in to your HubSpot developer account, then connect the HubSpot command-line tool to it.
steps.technical: Install @hubspot/cli (v7.6.0 or later), then run `hs account auth` and paste the personal access key when asked.
steps.whyHuman: Signing in and pasting the access key are yours to do.

steps.title: Create the app project
steps.plain: The agent runs one command that creates the app's files, choosing OAuth so many HubSpot accounts can connect.
steps.technical: `hs project create` > App > distribution: marketplace, auth: oauth. Set a unique `uid` in app-hsmeta.json; changing it later creates a different app.

steps.title: Add the redirect address and permissions
steps.plain: In the app's settings file, add your app's callback address and the HubSpot permissions your agent needs.
steps.technical: app-hsmeta.json: `auth.type: "oauth"`, `auth.redirectUrls: [<your callback URL>]`, `auth.requiredScopes: ["crm.objects.contacts.read", ...]`. Production redirect URLs must be https.

steps.title: Upload the app
steps.plain: The agent uploads the project, which builds the app in HubSpot.

steps.title: Store the client ID and secret in your app
steps.plain: Open the app in HubSpot, go to the Auth tab, and store the client ID and secret in your app's secret store or environment variables.
steps.technical: `hs project open` > Project Components > your app > Auth > Client credentials.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is a password for your app. Pasting it yourself keeps it out of any agent's chat history.

steps.title: Install it in a test account
steps.plain: Install it in a HubSpot test account through your app's sign-in flow. You will need to tick a box accepting an 'unverified app', because the app isn't listed yet.
steps.whyHuman: Installing needs a Super Admin of the account, and accepting the unverified-app warning is a judgment call.

steps.title: Use the access token directly (your own account only)
steps.plain: For a private app on your own account there is no sign-in flow: copy the app's access token and store it in your app's secret store or environment variables.
steps.technical: Set auth.type to "static" in app-hsmeta.json and remove redirectUrls. After hs project upload, copy the access token from the app's Auth tab.
steps.whyHuman: The token is a password for your account. Paste it yourself.

forks.condition: You want the 'unverified' warning gone (Marketplace listing)
forks.effect: You need at least 3 active installs in unrelated HubSpot accounts. HubSpot does a first review within 10 business days, and the full feedback cycle can run up to 60 days.

forks.condition: Only your own company's HubSpot account will connect
forks.effect: Use a private app with a static token instead of OAuth. No redirect addresses are needed.

nuances.title: Only Super Admins can install
nuances.detail: A regular HubSpot user at your customer can't connect the app.
nuances.ifStuck: Ask the customer's HubSpot Super Admin to do the first connection.

nuances.title: Is there a cap on installs before listing?
nuances.detail: Older HubSpot guidance limited unlisted apps to a small number of installs. The current docs we read don't mention a cap.
nuances.ifStuck: Ask HubSpot developer support before rolling out widely while unlisted.

evidence.note: Not stated on current pages. Not tested.

nuances.title: Access tokens last 30 minutes
nuances.detail: HubSpot access tokens expire after 1,800 seconds. Your code must renew them with the refresh token.
nuances.ifStuck: If calls start failing about 30 minutes after sign-in, check that your code refreshes the token.

config.redirectUriNote: Add your callback URL to auth.redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json.

useCases.label: Work in your customers' HubSpot accounts
useCases.summary: Built with the HubSpot CLI. No review, but installers accept an 'unverified app' warning until you list on the Marketplace.

useCases.label: Only your own company's HubSpot
useCases.summary: Use a private app with a static token. No OAuth redirect needed.

composio.note: You can connect users today with Composio's own HubSpot app while yours is set up or in review. Users see 'Composio' on the consent screen, rate limits are shared with other Composio customers, and polling triggers run at most every 15 minutes. Switch to your own app when it is ready.

existingApp.summary: Add your agent's callback address to auth.redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json if it differs, run hs project upload, and reuse the client ID and secret.

reReviewTriggers.effect: HubSpot treats it as a different app, so existing installs do not carry over. Keep the uid.
Accounts that already installed the app need to reinstall to grant the new scopes.

evidence.note: Not stated on the pages we read.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: Your app is listed on the HubSpot Marketplace
reReviewTriggers.effect: Listing changes go back through HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality review.

evidence.note: Inferred from the listing process; not stated for changes.

blockers.symptom: You can't list on the App Marketplace yet
blockers.cause: Listing needs at least three active installs: HubSpot accounts unconnected to your company that made successful API calls through your app in the last 30 days.
blockers.fix: Install the app directly for three customer accounts first, using your install link, and keep them active before you submit.

blockers.symptom: Your listing is set back to Draft or rejected
blockers.cause: Missing, incorrect or misleading listing details, dead links, or scopes your app requests but does not use.
blockers.fix: Apply the feedback from the Ecosystem Quality team, remove unused scopes or mark them optional, and resubmit. The first review takes up to 10 business days; the whole cycle should finish within 60 days. Submit one app at a time: extra submissions are rejected automatically.
